title: Sectors of the Economy and Functions of a Business
summary: The primary, secondary and tertiary sectors of the economy and how they link, the formal and informal sectors, and the eight functions of a business.

notes.text: The three sectors of the economy

rows: Takes raw materials directly from nature
Processes raw materials into finished or semi-finished products (manufacturing and construction)
Car factories, bakeries, sugar mills, steelworks, building houses
Shops (retail), banks, transport, tourism, education, healthcare

notes.title: How the sectors link: a wooden table
notes.problem: Show how the three sectors are involved in producing and selling a wooden table.
steps: Primary: a forestry company plants and cuts down pine trees.
Secondary: a sawmill cuts the timber; a furniture factory makes the table.
Tertiary: a truck transports it; a furniture shop sells it; a bank provides loans.
notes.answer: All three sectors depend on each other.

notes.text: In South Africa, the **tertiary sector** contributes the largest share of the economy (GDP) and jobs, followed by the secondary and then the primary sector. Mining and farming are still very important for exports and rural jobs.

rows: Businesses are registered with CIPC and SARS
Not registered; small and often run from home or the street
Pay taxes and follow labour laws
Examples: street vendors, spaza shops, car washes, hairdressers working from home

notes.label: Key idea
notes.text: The informal sector provides millions of South Africans with an income and is often a first step towards a formal business.
The eight functions of a business

rows: Planning, organising, leading and controlling the whole business; setting goals
Recording, storing and processing information: filing, record-keeping, computer systems
Raising capital, budgeting, controlling money, investing, paying accounts
Buying raw materials, stock and equipment of the right quality and quantity at the best price
Turning inputs into goods or services; quality control
Identifying customer needs, pricing, advertising, promotion and distribution (the 4 Ps: product, price, place, promotion)
Recruiting, selecting, training and paying staff; looking after their well-being
Building a good image of the business with the community and media; social responsibility projects

notes.text: In a small business, the owner may perform all these functions. In a large business, each function is usually a separate **department** with its own manager.

notes.title: Matching tasks to functions
notes.problem: A spaza shop owner does these tasks: orders stock, puts up posters, pays the electricity bill and hires a helper. Which function does each belong to?
steps: Posters promote the shop, so that is **marketing**.
Paying bills and managing money is the **financial** function.
notes.answer: Purchasing, marketing, financial and human resources.
